transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... people keep acting like I'm just imagining things. But I know what I see. The hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house. They even keep an eye on my cleaning routes when I'm at work. I know they're doing it to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. It's just frustrating that nobody believes me, so I guess that's why I was told to come in.
How long have you had the feeling that people are watching your house and monitoring your work routes?
Well, it's been about 11 months now. The feeling that people are watching us, and... well, the voices, too. They've both been happening for right around 11 months.
During these 11 months, have you also had periods where you felt very depressed, or unusually elated/energetic, along with hearing the voices and feeling watched?

Well, yes, I have. There were a few weeks where I was... well, I just had a whole lot of energy. I was sleeping very little and just running constantly from my cleaning jobs to doing church errands. And during those specific weeks, I was also hearing that woman's voice, and feeling certain that people were monitoring my routes. So, yes, they definitely happened at the same time.

Outside of those high-energy weeks, have there been times—lasting two weeks or more—when you were not feeling especially energetic or elated, but you were still hearing the voice or still feeling that people were watching you?

Yes, there was. There was a quieter spell for several weeks, actually. I wasn't rushing around so much, and I was sleeping a lot more. But even during that time, I still heard the voice... usually right by the kitchen window. And I still knew for a fact that the agency was watching us. So, yes, the watching and the voice didn't stop just because my energy slowed down.
During those weeks when you had a lot of energy and were sleeping very little, how would you describe your mood—were you feeling unusually happy, elated, or irritable, more than your usual self?

Well, during those times, I'd say my mood is... I feel really bright and strong, like I can just handle absolutely everything that comes my way. But at the same time, if my husband or one of my cleaning clients questions me or gets in my way, I end up snapping at them. And I snap much harder than I actually mean to. So it's a mix of feeling really good but also getting irritated pretty easily.
During that quieter, low-energy period when you were sleeping more, did you also feel unusually sad, hopeless, or down, or was your mood actually pretty normal at that time?

I wouldn't really say I felt sad or... or hopeless. My mood was actually pretty normal, I think. I was just tired. Like I said, I was sleeping a lot more and taking it easy, but I didn't feel down in the dumps or anything like that. Just quiet.
I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch that. Could you repeat the question?
